newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm in line with bunds, focus on U.S.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm in line with bunds, focus on U.S.

text.p: Irish government bonds firmed in thin late trade on Monday in line with German bunds as the market awaited the release of key economic data from the U.S. later in the week, dealers said.
Wednesday sees the release of November producer prices data while November consumer prices numbers are expected out on Thursday.
"Those numbers will be of interest to the market after last Friday's collapse," one dealer said.
"If the numbers are good then maybe Greenspan's comments of last week will be seen to have been mis-interpreted," the dealer added.

By 1555 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had firmed 55 pence from Friday's close at 101.70 to yield 5.99 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had gained 70 pence from the close at 108.75 to yield 6.62 percent.
Dealers said German bunds had pushed ahead of T-notes on spreads as both markets regained a steadier footing after last Friday's tailspin.

A close eye is also being kept on the Nuremberg meeting between German Chancellor Kohl and the French President Chirac to iron out tensions ahead of the EU Dublin summit on December 13-14, dealers said.
